project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop a reusable integration framework and kit for deploying artificial intelligence robotics in factories and other industrial settings.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Develop a modular way to integrate artificial intelligence robots into operating industrial systems. Demonstrate it across distinct uses and include compatible interfaces, adoption tools and relevant safety tests.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Industrial users and integrators need a repeatable way to connect robots to existing technology and workflows without rebuilding the entire system for each use.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Provide the integration framework and kit, reusable datasets and benchmark tasks, an adoption guide, and contributions to standards and practical certification guidance.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Speed adoption of safe and reusable robotic systems, especially for smaller businesses. The framework should help European users bring components from different developers together.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Publish practical adoption guidance and contribute to open standards where relevant. Use the European shared artificial intelligence platform and coordinate with the European industry and research partnership for artificial intelligence, data and robotics.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Build a team that brings robotics developers, system integrators and industrial users together. The topic restricts where participants can be established and who can control them.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Coordinate reusable modules, standards work, demonstrators and user guidance. Set aside tasks for cooperation with the European partnership for artificial intelligence, data and robotics.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on industrial robotics integration and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can validate a reusable robotic integration framework in a qualifying industrial pilot. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could validate a reusable robotic integration framework in a qualifying industrial pilot as an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant). It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could validate a reusable robotic integration framework in a qualifying industrial pilot. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The call restricts foreign control even for Dutch entities. A valid guarantee may be required, and entities controlled from China cannot use that route.

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could supply an industrial inspection or maintenance use case with a manufacturing partner. The work would need to validate reusable integration within one of the qualifying industrial pilots.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Develop reusable ways to integrate and deploy robotic technology. Existing robotics components can be used within the modular framework and its demonstrators.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The innovation is in integration architecture, interoperability, data and training protocols, safe commissioning and adoption tools for industrial users.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Start with technologies validated in a laboratory. Develop and test the integration kit and validate it in at least three real industrial pilots.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 7 (technology readiness level: a prototype demonstrated in operation) by project end. The work is expected to start at TRL 4 (technology readiness level: technology validated in a laboratory).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Validate the framework in at least three distinct real-world industrial pilots, covering smaller and larger businesses. Connect virtual testbeds where relevant.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Make the kit integrate different hardware and software modules with operating industrial systems. Where relevant, link pilots to digital twins (virtual test environments) and use recognised open standards.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Use at least three real industrial pilots in different scenarios to demonstrate that the framework transfers. Share reusable datasets and benchmark tasks under the relevant data and intellectual property rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: The project should bridge technology suppliers, system integrators and industrial end users. Prepare practical adoption guidance for small and medium-sized enterprises and other users.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Follow European data protection and intellectual property rules when sharing datasets. Build in safe testing and document any guarantees required when an applicant is controlled from an ineligible country.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 18 million for industrial robotics integration. It expects 1 award.
- Grant request: around EUR 18 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · p. 31 · Overview of this call
Apply AI: AI-Driven Robotics for Industry: Enabling System Integration and Adoption (IA) (Partnership in AI, Data and Robotics) · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards industrial robotics integration.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for industrial robotics integration using the cost categories allowed by the grant. The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) specifies how those costs can be claimed.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Personnel, purchases and eligible subcontracting.
- Overheads and value added tax (tax on purchases): The indirect-cost rate (overheads such as general office expenses) is 25% of the eligible direct-cost base after exclusions. value added tax is eligible where it is unrecoverable and the cost otherwise qualifies.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
EU Annotated Grant Agreement · p. 143 · Value added tax
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Digital, Industry and Space · pp. 151–154 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for industrial robotics integration around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Usually pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then interim payments linked to reporting and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for the mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for industrial robotics integration through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 18 March 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 17 November 2026.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for industrial robotics integration.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting industrial robotics integration is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months after the deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): The indicative signature date is around eight months after the deadline.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for industrial robotics integration.
- Application form: Complete Part A online and upload Part B as a fixed-format document with the required annexes.
- Registration: Enter a participant identification code for each beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entity (organisations legally linked to funded partners).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Participant Register

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Industrial robotics integration proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 per criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Weighting: Impact is multiplied by 1.5 for the ranking.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Industrial robotics applicants must meet the topic’s country and ownership-control rules.
- Conditional — Other countries associating in 2026–2027: Check topic eligibility in the participating-countries list at submission. The association agreement must apply at grant signature.
